doc.title: Jerry Dodgion interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 9, 1996

chapter: New York studio and recording work
title: Joe Williams and the 'rehearsal band' label
summary: Remembering Joe Williams from the Basie band in Las Vegas, he says Thad and Mel hated the term 'rehearsal band'.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Joe Williams: the singer with Basie

blocks.x: I wanted to mention this one record here that was done with Thad and Joe.
Remember that one? I think you played on that one too.

Oh, with Joe Williams. Oh, now he’s another special case. Oh, man. We met when I was with Red Norvo we played Las Vegas a lot, and when the band started coming to the Flamingo there, they’d come in for three or four weeks at a time sometimes. And so we met Joe, and he’s a really beautiful person, and he was part of the band. He was not a star with the band. I mean they traveled together these guys, and they roomed together, and he was just like one of the guys in the band. You know, there was a humanity thing happening with the Basie band that was just wonderful. It was just a joy to watch, and to be able to touch it a little bit was great for me. On this particular date, you know when we made this it was so funny with Thad and Mel’s band whenever — we didn’t rehearse very much. And in some of the chronicles they say it was a rehearsal band and then it became a band. It was never a rehearsal band, and Thad and Mel hated the word “rehearsal band.” They started the band to have a band. And when people say, “This is a rehearsal band,” they hated it. It’s not true. I mean Duke Pearson’s band rehearsed every week for a year and they never called him a “rehearsal band.” Thad and Mel had two rehearsals and went into the Vanguard and they called it a “rehearsal band.” I mean that was a very unfair — I mean it was no big deal to me, but to them it was really, you know?
I guess they just meant that the band didn’t tour around the country. I mean gee a gig at the Vanguard is hardly a rehearsal.
